question: Three similar breaker poles read 40, 48, and 70 µΩ. No manufacturer limit is published. Which reading does the 50-percent-of-the-lowest rule tell you to investigate?
choices: 40 µΩ, because it is the lowest
48 µΩ
70 µΩ
None; all are under 100 µΩ
explanation: Threshold is 1.5 times the lowest value: 40 × 1.5 = 60 µΩ. 70 µΩ is over that screen. 48 µΩ is not. There is no universal 100 µΩ ceiling in the ATS wording.

question: Why does a DLRO use a Kelvin (four-wire) connection?
choices: So the test can be done at 10 kV
So lead resistance and most clip drop are left out of the voltage measurement
So the meter reads megohms instead of microhms
So all three phases can be tested at once
explanation: Current uses one pair of leads. Voltage is sensed on a second pair inside those points, so the leads are not part of the ohm reading. Two-wire ohms on a microhm joint mostly measures the leads.
reference: Kelvin measurement practice; ATS contact-resistance tests assume a low-resistance ohmmeter

question: ATS 7.2.2.D.8 on liquid-filled transformer winding resistance says temperature-corrected values shall compare within:
choices: 0.5% of the calculated turns ratio
2% of previous results or of the adjacent phases
50% of the lowest phase
5% of nameplate impedance
explanation: The winding-resistance screen is two percent, after temperature correction, against a previous test or the adjacent phases. One-half percent is the turns-ratio rule. Fifty percent is the bolted-connection rule. Three percent shows up on leakage reactance, not here.

question: A 200-foot low-voltage busway has no manufacturer insulation-resistance value. ATS 7.4.D.2.a minimum, corrected to the 100-foot basis, is:
choices: 100 MΩ
2 MΩ
0.5 MΩ
200 MΩ
explanation: Minimum megohms = 100 / length in feet = 100/200 = 0.5 MΩ. A shorter run has a higher minimum. Do not apply a withstand until the reading is above that floor.

question: On a four-wire micro-ohmmeter the potential clips belong:
choices: Outside the current clips, on the leads
Inside the current clips, on the joint itself
On the same stud as the ground lead only
One on the joint and one on the test-set chassis
explanation: Current enters outside. Voltage is read between the inner clips, so the drop in the current leads is ignored. Reversing that order puts lead resistance back into the reading.
reference: AEMC 6240 user manual, per manufacturer instructions

question: A two-wire ohmmeter on a 50 µΩ bus joint typically:
choices: Matches a Kelvin reading within 1 µΩ
Reads high, because the leads are in the measurement
Reads the insulation resistance
Cannot be used below 10 A
explanation: Lead resistance is milliohms. The joint is microhms. Four-wire is how the AEMC 6240 and every other serious low-resistance ohmmeter drop the leads out. Then you still compare with similar joints under the 50 percent rule if the manufacturer is silent.
reference: AEMC 6240 user manual, per manufacturer instructions; ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.4.D.1
